en: The *Śrīgaṇeśapañcaratna*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda.
He who joyfully takes up the water of darkness, who is the eternal achiever of liberation, who is adorned by the moon, who protects the world with his grace,
who is the sole leader of those without a leader, and who has destroyed the elephant-like Daityas.
I bow to that Vināyaka, who destroys the auspicious and the inauspicious for those who prostrate before him. ||1||

I bow to the Lord of the Gods, the Lord of Treasures, the Lord of the Elephant, and the Lord of the Gaṇas— He who is exceedingly terrifying to his enemies, resplendent like the newly risen sun, the destroyer of the gods' foes, the deliverer from the great distress of those who bow to Him.
I take refuge in that Maheśvara, who is higher than the highest and eternal. 2.
The benefactor of all the worlds, who has cast down the elephants that are the Daityas; whose belly is free from fear; the most excellent one with a face like a choice elephant; the imperishable;
the source of compassion, the source of forgiveness, the source of joy, and the source of glory.
I pay homage to the radiant Manaskāra, who has been saluted by all. ||3||
The cleanser of the suffering of those who possess nothing, the vessel for the words of the ancients, the joy of the primordial enemy of Tripura, the devourer of the pride of the enemies of the gods,
terrifying to the world of manifestation, and the ornament of Arjuna and others— [I bow to that Lord].
I worship the ancient elephant, who prevents the flow of ichor from his temples. 4.
To the son of Kāntā, who possesses the splendor of exceedingly beautiful teeth, whose form is inconceivable, who is without end, and who cuts away all obstacles—
to Him who dwells eternally within the hearts of yogis; [I bow].
I constantly meditate upon that very One-Tusked Lord. ||5||
He who daily recites with devotion the *Mahāgaṇeśapañcaratna* at dawn, while remembering Gaṇeśvara in his heart,
attains freedom from disease, freedom from defects, excellent literary skill, and the possession of virtuous sons.
He soon attains his desired lifespan and the eightfold prosperity.
